data.gender_notes: Naemi is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Naomi means 'comfort' or 'consolation'. In the Old Testament, Naomi was the name of a woman who, after suffering many trials, was comforted by the return of her son and grandson. The name Naemi carries the meaning “Comfort or Consolation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Naemi usually hope their child will grow to embody comfort or consolation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of comfort and solace, reminding us of God's presence and healing power.
data.etymology: Naemi belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Comfort or Consolation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Naemi total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: נעמי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נעמי הוא שם עברי שמקורו בספר רות. הוא נגזר מהמילה 'נעמה' שפירושה 'עצי', 'נעימות', 'שמחה'. השם נעמי מוזכר בתנ'ך כדמותה של אשתו של אלימלך ואמו של מחלון וכיליון. השם נעמי הוא סמלי לשמחה ולשובח הנעמתו של האל.

in_greek.name: Ναεμι
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ναεμι είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος נעמי (Naomi). Στη Βίβλο, η Ναεμι ήταν η γυναίκα του Ελιμέλεχ και η μητέρα του Μαχλών και του Κιλιών. Το όνομα αυτό προέρχεται από τη λέξη 'ναά' που σημαίνει 'προσάρεστο' ή 'χάρη'. Στην παράδοση των Χριστιανών, το όνομα Ναεμι συμβολίζει τη χαρά και την ανανέωση.

in_latin.name: Naemi
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Naemi in traditione Christiana est forma Latina nominis hebraici נעמי (Naomi). In Biblia, Naemi fuit uxor Elimelech et mater Machlonis et Chelionis. Nomen Naemi derivatur a voce hebraica 'na'ah' quod significat 'amoenum' vel 'gaudium'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Naemi habebat significationem spiritualem de gaudio et restauratione.

in_english.name: Naemi
in_english.long_meaning: The name Naemi originates from the Hebrew name נעמי (Naomi), meaning 'pleasant', 'joyful', or 'delightful'. In the Bible, Naomi was the wife of Elimelech and the mother of Mahlon and Chilion. The name is derived from the Hebrew word 'na'ah', which means 'to be pleasant' or 'to be delightful'. In Christian tradition, the name Naemi symbolizes joy, pleasantness, and spiritual restoration. It has been used across various cultures and is associated with positive personality traits such as kindness, warmth, and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Naomi can bring comfort and solace to those who hear it. It is a name with a deeply personal and emotional resonance, as it speaks of the healing power of love, family, and hope in the face of hardship. In a world where many seek comfort in fleeting earthly pleasures, the name Naomi serves as a gentle reminder of the longer-lasting, spiritual comfort that comes from God.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Naomi holds deep spiritual significance, as it speaks to the reality of both human suffering and divine comfort. It is a reminder that even in the midst of pain and sorrow, God is ever present and ready to console us. The name Naomi also highlights the transformative power of God's love, as seen in the life of the biblical Naomi who was comforted by the return of her son and grandson. In this way, the name Naomi serves as a powerful reminder of the promise of God's consolation, and the hope that no matter what trials we may face in life, He will be with us, and will bring us comfort in due time.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Naomi means "pleasantness" or "gentleness" in Hebrew. It is a name filled with warmth and kindness, symbolizing a nurturing and comforting spirit. In Christian tradition, Naomi represents the loving and supportive mother figure, embodying God's grace and compassion.

biblical_reference.note: Naomi is a central figure in the Book of Ruth, a story of loyalty, faith, and redemption.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament book of Ruth, there is a Moabite woman named Naomi. She was originally called Mara (bitter) but was given the name Naomi (pleasant) after her bitterness turned to joy upon the return of her son, Obed, and grandson, Jesse, who would later become the ancestors of King David.
historical_references.context: The Book of Ruth is part of the Ketuvim (Writings) division of the Hebrew Bible, and is traditionally attributed to the prophet Samuel.

historical_references.reference: In the Middle Ages, particularly in France and Flanders, there was a female saint named Naemias (or Naemisia). She was believed to have been a virgin martyr, and her feast day is celebrated on December 8th.
historical_references.context: The exact details of Saint Naemias' life are not known, and there are several conflicting stories about her origins and martyrdom. Some sources claim she was a Roman noblewoman who converted to Christianity, while others say she was a Syrian or Persian princess. She is often depicted with a palm branch or a palm leaf, symbolizing martyrdom.
